1. Remember the little things. Their coffee order, their sister's name, the exam they were nervous about. Small details show people they matter to you.
2. Make people laugh. Shared laughter creates strong memories. You don't need to be a comedian, just relaxed enough to enjoy the moment.
3. Show up when it counts. Birthdays, hospital visits, moving days. People never forget who was there for them in big moments. Keep it simple and genuine.
4. Have a signature. A handshake, a phrase, a style, a dish you always bring. A small personal touch makes you easy to remember. Make yours special.
5. Always have something interesting to share. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and people remember the stories I tell.
slides.texte_sophia: 5. I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. People remember the stories I tell.

slides.texte_overlay: 6. Send the message first. A thank you after dinner, a "good luck today" before their interview. Thoughtful messages stay in people's minds.
7. Leave on a high. End conversations while they're still fun. People remember the last moment they spent with you. Short, warm and genuine goodbyes stay with people for a long time.
